\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{নর্দমা} (nôrdômā)}{নর্দমা (nôrdômā)}]{\bn{নর্দমা} (nôrdômā) — a drain; a gutter}

\label{lesson:BN-C413-nordoma}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for a lamp post, then the Bengali for to climb over.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{নর্দমা}}
\textbf{\bn{নর্দমা}} — \emph{nôrdômā} — \textquotedblleft{}a drain; a gutter\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{আমাদের} \bn{গলির} \bn{নর্দমা} \bn{খোলা।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{āmāder gôlir nôrdômā kholā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The drain in our lane is open.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{নর্দমা}} (\emph{nôrdômā}) is the open drain along a lane; its origin is not settled, and CDIAL gives no Bengali form for it.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{nôrdômā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{nôrdômā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{āmāder gôlir nôrdômā kholā.} — The drain in our lane is open.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Bengali for a lamp post, then the Bengali for to climb over, then say \emph{nôrdômā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \bn{নর্দমা} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A drain; a gutter\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{পাইপ} (pāip)}{পাইপ (pāip)}]{\bn{পাইপ} (pāip) — a pipe}

\label{lesson:BN-C413-paip}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for to climb over, then the Bengali for a drain.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{পাইপ}}
\textbf{\bn{পাইপ}} — \emph{pāip} — \textquotedblleft{}a pipe\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{মিস্ত্রি} \bn{নর্দমার} \bn{পুরনো} \bn{পাইপ} \bn{বদলালেন।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{mistri nôrdômār purôno pāip bôdlālen.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The plumber replaced the old drainpipe.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{পাইপ}} (\emph{pāip}) is borrowed from English \emph{pipe}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{pāip}, once more

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Bengali for to climb over, then the Bengali for a drain, then say \emph{pāip} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{ডাস্টবিন} (ḍāsṭbin)}{ডাস্টবিন (ḍāsṭbin)}]{\bn{ডাস্টবিন} (ḍāsṭbin) — a dustbin}

\label{lesson:BN-C413-dastbin}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for a drain, then the Bengali for a pipe.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{ডাস্টবিন}}
\textbf{\bn{ডাস্টবিন}} — \emph{ḍāsṭbin} — \textquotedblleft{}a dustbin\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{রোজ} \bn{সকালে} \bn{একটা} \bn{গাড়ি} \bn{এসে} \bn{ডাস্টবিন} \bn{খালি} \bn{করে।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{roj sôkāle ekṭā gāṛi ese ḍāsṭbin khāli kôre.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Every morning a truck comes and empties the dustbins.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{ডাস্টবিন}} (\emph{ḍāsṭbin}) is borrowed from English \emph{dustbin}.
\end{cousinweb}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{ময়লা} (môylā)}{ময়লা (môylā)}]{\bn{ময়লা} (môylā) — dirt; rubbish; dirty}

\label{lesson:BN-C413-moyla}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for a pipe, then the Bengali for a dustbin.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{ময়লা}}
\textbf{\bn{ময়লা}} — \emph{môylā} — \textquotedblleft{}dirt; rubbish; dirty\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{ময়লা} \bn{ডাস্টবিনে} \bn{ফেলতে} \bn{হবে।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{môylā ḍāsṭbine phelte hôbe.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Rubbish has to go in the dustbin.
\end{quote}

Also the adjective dirty, of clothes and water: \bn{ময়লা} \bn{জামা}, a dirty shirt.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{ময়লা}} (\emph{môylā}) is inherited: CDIAL lists Bengali \emph{mayalā}, \textquotedblleft{}dirt\textquotedblright{}, under the reconstructed \emph{malin-}, \textquotedblleft{}dirty\textquotedblright{}, beside Sanskrit \emph{malina} (CDIAL 9904).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{môylā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{môylā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{môylā ḍāsṭbine phelte hôbe.} — Rubbish has to go in the dustbin.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Bengali for a pipe, then the Bengali for a dustbin, then say \emph{môylā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{জঞ্জাল} (jônjāl)}{জঞ্জাল (jônjāl)}]{\bn{জঞ্জাল} (jônjāl) — junk; clutter; a heap of rubbish}

\label{lesson:BN-C413-jonjal}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for a dustbin, then the Bengali for dirt.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{জঞ্জাল}}
\textbf{\bn{জঞ্জাল}} — \emph{jônjāl} — \textquotedblleft{}junk; clutter; a heap of rubbish\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{নর্দমাটা} \bn{জঞ্জালে} \bn{ভর্তি।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{nôrdômāṭā jônjāle bhôrti.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The drain is choked with junk.
\end{quote}

Old things piled up and in the way: \bn{ঘরের} \bn{জঞ্জাল}, the clutter in a room.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{জঞ্জাল}} (\emph{jônjāl}) is inherited: CDIAL lists Bengali \emph{jañjāl}, \textquotedblleft{}disorder, rubbish\textquotedblright{}, under the reconstructed \emph{jañjāla} (CDIAL 5085).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{jônjāl}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{jônjāl}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{nôrdômāṭā jônjāle bhôrti.} — The drain is choked with junk.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Bengali for a dustbin, then the Bengali for dirt, then say \emph{jônjāl} again
\end{itemize}
